To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Employee brand equity is driven by both cognitive (i.e. brand knowledge) and affective (i.e. identification) routes and is significantly related to brand value dissemination and employee customer orientation.

(1) employee based brand equity can be driven by brand knowledge and brand identity, (2) employee perceptions of their supervisors' brand management behavior can drive employee based brand equity and (3) employee based brand can be a driver of brand value dissemination and employee customer orientation.

employees who perceive their supervisors' brand management practices as being consistent with their own values and who are able to identify with their organization's brand will be more motivated to engage in brand-related behaviors that will benefit the brand.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBBE is a key antecedent of brand value dissemination and a key mediator of the impact of supervisor leadership behaviors on employee customer orientation.
employees' responses to internal branding are driven by the extent to which their supervisors demonstrate brand leadership behaviors and are focused on their development.
EBBE is an important construct for service firms and its antecedents are not only the brand leadership behaviors but also supervisors' focus on employees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brand is a powerful tool for managing employees and their interactions with external stakeholders.
EBBE can be developed by focusing on employees' brand knowledge and brand identity and by enhancing the brand's value to employees through brand leadership behaviors.
the internal brand is a critical organizational asset that is largely ignored by both marketing and human resources scholars.
